subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should OpenClaw promote successful compaction completion into an authoritative reconciliation boundary for session-derived state beyond compactionCount?
rationale: Current main has a narrow count repair, but deciding whether token snapshots, status freshness, memory-flush state, auth-profile markers, or channel recovery signals should converge through the same event is an ownership and session-state semantics choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Design a bounded reconciliation layer
options.body: Define one helper or event for monotonic compaction-derived state and enroll only fields whose truth is successful compaction completion.

options.title: Keep the count-only repair
options.body: Leave compactionCount as the only late-success reconciliation target and narrow or close the broader follow-up if more state should stay on existing paths.

options.title: Split by state surface
options.body: Track token/status snapshots, memory flush gating, and channel recovery as separate follow-ups instead of one shared boundary.

recommendation.title: Design a bounded reconciliation layer
recommendation.body: Define one helper or event for monotonic compaction-derived state and enroll only fields whose truth is successful compaction completion.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman reviewed and co-authored the merged narrow fix, so they are the strongest available routing candidate for deciding whether that boundary should expand.
